title: GH&B Portfolio Management Lead (LATAM)
skills: Global Hospital & Biosimilars (GH&B) makes the products that are the foundation of hospital care — sterile injectables and biosimilars – that reach more than 100 million patients annually, generating $5 billion in revenue for Pfizer. These are not niche products; they are for when patients are at the most vulnerable, essential to access and acute care delivery worldwide.

GH&B is Pfizer's only truly end-to-end business, spanning from our 12 global manufacturing sites through to commercial in a single integrated organization. It was created to give this portfolio dedicated focus, clearer accountability, and a fit-for-purpose operating model — recognizing that GH&B's portfolio has different economics, customer dynamics, and execution needs than Pfizer's innovative business.
By bringing Commercial and Supply into one organization, GH&B enables faster decision-making, stronger prioritization, and expanded capabilities for this important portfolio.
Our ambition: Rebuild a healthy operation positioned to serve patients for generations to come.

The Portfolio Management Lead is the strategic owner of the cluster's product portfolio across biosimilars and generics (Oncology, Immunology/Inflammation), responsible for driving portfolio prioritization, go-to-market design, launch sequencing, and lifecycle optimization across all cluster markets. The role translates global portfolio strategy into cluster-specific execution plans, ensuring the right products reach the right markets at the right time -- balancing growth ambition with resource constraints and competitive realities.

This is a build-and-shape role: the Portfolio Management Lead will establish portfolio governance and decision-making frameworks from the ground up, identify white-space growth opportunities, and orchestrate cross-functional launch readiness in a newly formed cluster operating model.
Portfolio Strategy & Prioritization
Own the cluster portfolio strategy across biosimilars and generics; prioritize products by market opportunity, competitive dynamics, and margin contribution
Translate global portfolio and lifecycle decisions into cluster-specific roadmaps, calibrating to local market realities (regulatory timelines, competitive landscapes, payer requirements)
Conduct portfolio gap analysis and white-space identification to inform growth opportunities and in-licensing/expansion discussions with Global
Manage portfolio rationalization decisions – recommend product additions, withdrawals, or re-sequencing based on evolving market intelligence
Design go-to-market approaches tailored to cluster archetypes -- adapting to contract-driven, tender-driven, or partner/distributor-led environments
Define the commercial model per product and market: channel mix, customer targeting (hospital pharmacy, tender bodies, payers, wholesalers), and the resourcing required to execute

Drive launch readiness and launch sequencing for new product introductions, coordinating cross-functional workstreams (Medical, Regulatory, Supply, Market Access, Tenders & Contracting) and optimizing timing against competitive windows, supply availability, and market access milestones
Identify and develop growth opportunities through portfolio expansion, geographic extension, and new indication pull-through
Assess and recommend entry strategies for underpenetrated markets within the cluster
Collaborate with Global Portfolio Strategy on pipeline visibility and early commercial input for assets relevant to the cluster
Lead business case development for portfolio investments, working with Finance and Commercial Performance to model revenue scenarios
Decide which portfolio assets are best commercialized through partners or distributors versus direct Pfizer execution, and recommend the partnering model by asset and market
Drive partner selection process: define selection criteria, lead evaluation and due diligence, and recommend commercial terms for Cluster Lead approval (incl. Legal, Finance, and Compliance)

description:
Getting to know GH&B


Global Hospital & Biosimilars (GH&B) makes the products that are the foundation of hospital care — sterile injectables and biosimilars – that reach more than 100 million patients annually, generating $5 billion in revenue for Pfizer. These are not niche products; they are for when patients are at the most vulnerable, essential to access and acute care delivery worldwide. 
GH&B is Pfizer's only truly end-to-end business, spanning from our 12 global manufacturing sites through to commercial in a single integrated organization. It was created to give this portfolio dedicated focus, clearer accountability, and a fit-for-purpose operating model — recognizing that GH&B's portfolio has different economics, customer dynamics, and execution needs than Pfizer's innovative business. 
By bringing Commercial and Supply into one organization, GH&B enables faster decision-making, stronger prioritization, and expanded capabilities for this important portfolio. 
Our ambition: Rebuild a healthy operation positioned to serve patients for generations to come. 


Use Your Power for Purpose


The Portfolio Management Lead is the strategic owner of the cluster's product portfolio across biosimilars and generics (Oncology, Immunology/Inflammation), responsible for driving portfolio prioritization, go-to-market design, launch sequencing, and lifecycle optimization across all cluster markets. The role translates global portfolio strategy into cluster-specific execution plans, ensuring the right products reach the right markets at the right time -- balancing growth ambition with resource constraints and competitive realities. 
This is a build-and-shape role: the Portfolio Management Lead will establish portfolio governance and decision-making frameworks from the ground up, identify white-space growth opportunities, and orchestrate cross-functional launch readiness in a newly formed cluster operating model. 


What You Will Achieve


Portfolio Strategy & Prioritization
Own the cluster portfolio strategy across biosimilars and generics; prioritize products by market opportunity, competitive dynamics, and margin contribution
Translate global portfolio and lifecycle decisions into cluster-specific roadmaps, calibrating to local market realities (regulatory timelines, competitive landscapes, payer requirements)
Conduct portfolio gap analysis and white-space identification to inform growth opportunities and in-licensing/expansion discussions with Global
Manage portfolio rationalization decisions – recommend product additions, withdrawals, or re-sequencing based on evolving market intelligence


Go-to-Market Design


Design go-to-market approaches tailored to cluster archetypes -- adapting to contract-driven, tender-driven, or partner/distributor-led environments
Define the commercial model per product and market: channel mix, customer targeting (hospital pharmacy, tender bodies, payers, wholesalers), and the resourcing required to execute
Drive launch readiness and launch sequencing for new product introductions, coordinating cross-functional workstreams (Medical, Regulatory, Supply, Market Access, Tenders & Contracting) and optimizing timing against competitive windows, supply availability, and market access milestones


Growth Opportunities & Market Development


Identify and develop growth opportunities through portfolio expansion, geographic extension, and new indication pull-through
Assess and recommend entry strategies for underpenetrated markets within the cluster
Collaborate with Global Portfolio Strategy on pipeline visibility and early commercial input for assets relevant to the cluster
Lead business case development for portfolio investments, working with Finance and Commercial Performance to model revenue scenarios


Partnership & Alliance Management


Decide which portfolio assets are best commercialized through partners or distributors versus direct Pfizer execution, and recommend the partnering model by asset and market
Drive partner selection process: define selection criteria, lead evaluation and due diligence, and recommend commercial terms for Cluster Lead approval (incl. Legal, Finance, and Compliance)
Own the ongoing partner relationship – joint business planning, target setting, and volume and stock commitments — working within the SLA and governance parameters set at the cluster level
Track partner performance against agreed targets and re-assess, renegotiate, or exit arrangements where performance, compliance, or shifting portfolio priorities require it


Supply Interface & Demand Planning

Translate commercial forecasts and launch plans into supply requirements; escalate and manage supply constraint trade-offs across markets
Leverage the technical supply forecasts and analytics produced by the Commercial Performance to inform commercial demand planning, improve forecast accuracy, and flag constraint risk earlier


Cross-Functional Portfolio Governance


Establish and lead portfolio governance forums within the cluster -- including regular portfolio reviews, launch readiness gates, and lifecycle decision checkpoints
Coordinate with Pricing, Market Access, and Tenders & Contracting to ensure portfolio decisions are reflected in pricing corridors, tender strategies, and formulary submissions

Collaborate with the Commercial Performance Manager to ensure portfolio KPIs, revenue tracking, and competitive intelligence feed back into portfolio decisions


Technology & AI Enablement

Demonstrate strong personal digital literacy and AI fluency, modelling practical use of data, digital tools, and AI-enabled solutions

description:
About Us

Most AI is frozen in place - it doesn’t adapt to the world. We think that’s backwards. Our mandate is to build efficient intelligence that evolves in real-time. We bring together exceptional people with the drive and creativity to push the boundaries of continual adaptation. We’re looking for builders and creative thinkers ready to shape the next era of intelligence.

Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in accountability, initiative and shared success. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world. We operate with low egos, high velocity, and extreme ownership to build technology that expands access and benefits the many, not the few.

How We Work


Impact Over Activity: We are building a generational company. We value people who execute on ideas rather than comment from the sidelines. We believe our competitive edge lies in caring about excellence across the entire lifecycle - from research to product. No task is beneath anyone: no one is too senior to test the build, clean the data, or unblock a teammate. 
Vulnerable, Low-Ego Collaboration: We believe exceptional work comes from people who challenge, support and push one another to think bigger. Rapid iteration requires stepping into discomfort. We encourage bold, half-baked, and unorthodox ideas. When we disagree, we share feedback directly, never through side channels. 
Celebrate Decisively: Extraordinary effort should be deeply memorable. We celebrate milestones generously and publicly - via spot bonuses, team dinners, spontaneous gifts, and company-wide recognition - to fuel each other for the next sprint. 


The Role

Our vision is AI systems that are flexible, adaptable, and accessible to everyone. We believe efficiency is what makes this possible. It’s how we expand access and ensure innovation benefits the many, not the few.

You will be the engine room of Adaption's hackathon and community programs: the person who makes sure hundreds of moving parts land on time, every week, without anything slipping through the cracks.

Our vision is AI systems that are flexible, adaptable, and accessible to everyone. In 2027, a big part of how we reach builders is through hackathons, university partnerships, and developer events around the world. We are scaling that program fast, and we need someone who genuinely enjoys volume: dozens of organizers to contact, credits to coordinate, speakers to schedule, and follow-ups to chase.

This is a hands-on operations role. You'll work side by side with our growth team, take a large share of the day-to-day execution off their plates, and then make the whole machine faster, using AI tools and smart systems so that what took a day last month takes an hour this month.

You need to be relentlessly organized, fast, scrappy, and energized by getting things done.

What You’ll Do


Run high-volume outreach. Research and contact hackathon organizers, university groups, accelerators, and developer communities worldwide. Expect to manage outreach to 40+ partners a week and send 60+ personalized emails, then follow up until every thread is closed. 
Own hackathon logistics end to end. Coordinate sponsorship packages, API credits, prizes, and deadlines. Schedule and brief Adaption engineers who speak, judge, or mentor, and make sure they have what they need before they show up. 
Keep the program calendar. Maintain the master schedule of hackathons, events, launches, and deliverables against our 2027 roadmap. Know what's happening when, what's at risk, and what needs to move. 
Be the reliable point of contact. Join calls with organizers in India, Africa, Southeast Asia, Europe, and the Americas. Answer questions quickly and keep partners feeling looked after. 
Track everything. Keep our CRM and trackers clean and current: who we've contacted, what we've promised, what's due, and what results each event delivered. 
Automate as you go. Build AI agents, templates, and workflows to speed up research, outreach, and follow-up. When you do something twice, figure out how to do it better the third time. 
Lead community operations. Help run the logistics behind meetups, office hours, and webinars, and help keep our community spaces organized and up to date. 
Bring ideas, not just checkmarks. Once the machine is running, spot what's working and suggest new ways to scale our reach. 


Skills You’ll Bring

We look beyond traditional markers of experience. What matters most to us is what you’ve built and the impact you’ve had. We value demonstrable output, curiosity and alignment with our core values:

We care more about how you work than where you've worked. Great fits might come from events and program coordination, executive assistance, startup operations, partnerships, teaching, or any role where staying organized under pressure was the job.


2+ years in a fast-paced, detail-heavy role where you juggled many stakeholders and deadlines at once
Exceptionally organized: you carry a hundred details without dropping one, and you build systems so you don't have to rely on memory
Fast and clear written communication; you can write a friendly, effective outreach email in minutes
Comfortable with high volume and repetitive tasks, and you take pride in doing them well and faster each time
Genuinely curious about AI tools and eager to use them to automate your own work
Proactive and self-directed: you see what needs to happen next and do it without waiting to be asked
Comfortable working with people across cultures and time zones


Above all, we’re looking for great teammates who make work feel lighter and aren’t afraid to go out on a limb with bold ideas. You don’t need to be perfect, but you do need to be adaptable. We encourage you to apply, even if you don’t check every box.

Nice to Have


A general understanding of how hackathons or developer events work, whether you've attended, volunteered, or helped organize one
Experience with outreach tools, CRMs, or building simple automations (Zapier, Make, Airtable, or similar)
Startup or early-stage experience


What This Role Isn't

To save us both time: this isn't a social media, content, or developer advocacy role. Those are owned by other people on the team. You won't need to write code or be an AI expert. This role is about making our programs run brilliantly at scale.

What we offer

description:
THE ORGANIZATION

The Entrepreneurs’ Organization (EO) is a high-quality support network of 19,000 business founders and owners in 220 chapters and 80 countries worldwide. EO’s purpose is to move the world forward by unlocking the full potential of entrepreneurs. Since 1987, EO has helped entrepreneurs achieve transformational growth through the power of life-enhancing connections, shared experiences, and collaborative learning. Guided by EO’s core values: trust and respect, thirst for learning, think big, be bold, and together we grow, EO’s international staff collaborates successfully across diverse cultures. As an EO employee, you will gain access to the world’s top experts in entrepreneurship, grow beyond your perceived limits, and make breakthroughs as you refine and realize your personal goals. EO’s competitive total rewards package, flexible work environment, and generous professional development resources are frequently cited as among the most popular benefits of working at EO.




Position Summary

The Manager is responsible for the strategy, management, operations, and continued evolution of EO’s MyEO program and the Industry Community’s Industry Groups.

This role serves as the primary staff partner for MyEO leaders and Champions and leads the integration and evolution of MyEO experiences within OneEO. The Manager is responsible for ensuring that MyEO remains a flexible, member-led program while establishing the governance, processes, digital experiences, training, data, and operational structure needed to support the program globally.

The Manager works cross-functionally with Digital Communities, Technology, Governance, Legal, Marketing and Communications, regional teams, and other stakeholders to evolve the MyEO program. The role translates member and leader needs into program improvements, platform requirements, workflows, and scalable solutions.

Additionally, the role is part of the team that helps to plan, co-design, and execute global programs within the communities team. They will provide support to member leaders for Industry Groups which form part of the Industry Community.

This position combines program management, community engagement, digital platform management, stakeholder relationships, training and enablement, data analysis, and continuous improvement.




Essential Duties And Responsibilities

MyEO program management and strategy

Manage the MyEO program, including program strategy, priorities, roadmap, operating model, annual planning, and budget.
Develop and implement strategies that strengthen the MyEO member experience and increase participation in MyEO Groups and Events.
Establish program goals, success measures, and priorities based on member needs, organizational objectives, and program performance.
Identify opportunities to improve and evolve MyEO processes, services, tools, and experiences.
Maintain clear program standards, documentation, workflows, and ownership across MyEO activities.

MyEO evolution within OneEO

Lead the evolution of MyEO Groups and Events within OneEO.
Develop and maintain clear processes for MyEO Groups and Events operating within the evolving OneEO ecosystem.
Support flexible MyEO Group models, including groups operating within OneEO, groups using OneEO together with an external communication platform, and groups using an approved external communication platform while remaining represented within the MyEO experience in OneEO.
Lead testing and feedback initiatives with MyEO leaders and members and incorporate findings into program and platform improvements.
Maintain visibility into migration risks, exceptions, open decisions, and dependencies requiring cross-functional resolution.

MyEO Groups and Events

Oversee the end-to-end lifecycle and operating processes for MyEO Groups and Events.
Manage standards and workflows for MyEO Group creation, review, approval, onboarding, ongoing management, and closure.
Manage standards and workflows for MyEO Event creation, approval, risk review, promotion, member registration, and reporting.
Ensure appropriate processes are maintained for event risk waivers and other required program or governance requirements.
Oversee regular MyEO Group reviews and audits and identify required follow-up actions.
Partner with operational resources supporting group and event processing, member inquiries, reporting, documentation, and platform administration.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce manual work, and improve the member and Champion experience.

MyEO leadership and stakeholder management

Serve as the primary staff liaison to MyEO Experts, Chairs, Group Champions, Event Champions, and other MyEO member leaders.
Establish consistent communication and engagement with MyEO leaders to support planning, program delivery, issue resolution, and continuous improvement.
Provide continuity and institutional knowledge through annual MyEO leadership transitions.
Gather and translate member and leader feedback into program recommendations and operational improvements.
Support MyEO leaders in understanding program expectations, available tools, governance requirements, and opportunities to strengthen their Groups and Events.
Build productive relationships across global, regional, and chapter stakeholders involved in MyEO.

Community Management for Industry Groups

Develops goals for Industry Groups in line with community and department objectives that drive member engagement. Responsible for ensuring high-quality execution for assigned community goals, activities, learning opportunities, and member connection experiences.
Serves as staff design expert for member engagement opportunities (principally virtual). Brings relevant expertise in program design, event planning and logistics, communications and engagement experience to community initiatives. Supports and assigns staff support as needed.
Works with member leads and their leadership teams on strategic and tactical planning of engagement opportunities with the goal of engaging every member beyond their local chapter in meaningful ways. Serves as the staff liaison and operational partner for community and Industry group leaders, providing ideas, guidance, and ensuring that planned engagement adheres to EO standards.

Governance and program standards

Partner with Governance, Legal, and relevant staff teams to maintain appropriate governance and risk-management processes for MyEO Groups and Events.
Maintain clear decision criteria, responsibilities, escalation paths, and exceptions for program workflows.
Ensure MyEO Champions understand applicable EO policies, responsibilities, and program requirements.
Identify emerging program risks or policy questions and coordinate appropriate review and resolution.
Balance appropriate organizational standards with the flexibility and member-led nature of MyEO.

Training, onboarding, and enablement

Lead the development and delivery of the MyEO training and enablement strategy.
Lead or coordinate MyEO content for Chapter Officer Training for MyEO Experts and Chairs.
Develop onboarding and ongoing enablement for MyEO Group and Event Champions.
Maintain current training materials, user guides, facilitator resources, FAQs, SOPs, and program documentation.
Ensure training and documentation evolve alongside OneEO functionality and MyEO processes.
Partner with relevant EO teams to deliver training and support for members and leaders adopting new MyEO tools and workflows.

Member engagement and communications

Develop strategies to increase awareness, discovery, participation, and engagement in MyEO Groups and Events.
Partner with Marketing and Communications on MyEO campaigns, program announcements, stories, and member communications.
Support the development and direction of recurring MyEO communications.
Identify and share examples of successful MyEO Groups, Events, and Champions to encourage participation and peer learning.
Ensure MyEO communications clearly explain changes in program processes, technology, or member experiences.

Data, reporting, and insights

Establish and maintain MyEO performance measures for Groups, Events, participation, engagement, and program health.
Oversee regular MyEO reporting and provide insights and recommendations based on program data.
Maintain reliable data definitions and reporting processes across OneEO and other approved sources.
Develop approaches for gathering appropriate activity and participation data from MyEO Groups operating outside OneEO.
Lead improvements to MyEO reporting and data structures within OneEO.
Support the development of the MyEO Annual Report and other organizational reporting requirements.
Use data and member feedback to identify opportunities, risks, and priorities for continuous improvement.

Cross-functional collaboration and continuous improvement

Serve as the primary MyEO program partner to Digital Communities, Technology, Governance, Legal, Marketing and Communications, regional teams, and other EO functions.
Represent MyEO requirements and priorities in OneEO planning and development.
Coordinate decisions and implementation when platform or process changes affect MyEO members and leaders.
Maintain a prioritized roadmap of program, process, and technology improvements.
Lead or support pilots, testing, and implementation of new MyEO experiences, processes, and functionality.
Perform other duties and assignments as necessary.




Qualifications, Skills, And Knowledge Required

Required:

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
3+ years of experience in program management, community management, membership organizations, digital engagement, or related field.
Demonstrated experience managing complex programs involving multiple stakeholders, workstreams, and dependencies.
Experience working with digital community, membership, event, or collaboration platforms.
Experience developing and improving operational processes, workflows, and documentation.
Experience working with members, customers, volunteers, or community leaders.
Strong project management skills with demonstrated ability to manage priorities, timelines, risks, and deliverables.
Experience using data and qualitative feedback to evaluate program performance and inform decisions.
Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills.
Ability to work effectively across cultures, regions, and time zones.

Preferred:

Experience with online community platforms, including Hivebrite or similar technology.
Experience with event management processes and platforms.
Experience supporting platform migrations, technology implementations, or organizational change initiatives.
Experience developing and delivering training or enablement programs.
Experience working with volunteer leadership structures.
Bilingual or multilingual capabilities.

COMPETENCIES AND CHARACTERISTICS

Strong relationship management and stakeholder engagement skills.
Member-focused and service-oriented approach.
Collaborative self-starter with a high level of ownership and accountability.
Strong judgment and ability to navigate complex or ambiguous situations.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
Ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on program execution.
Comfortable managing multiple priorities in a global environment.

description:
Acerca del rol




Coordinador/a Incubadora Centros de Negocio




En este rol serás responsable de coordinar con la comunidad interna y externa la creación de empresas rentables, mediante un esquema de asesoría y mentoría alineado al proceso institucional de incubación. Impulsarás el desarrollo, formalización y puesta en marcha de microempresas, promoviendo la cultura del emprendimiento y generando impacto en la formación práctica de nuestros estudiantes, el fortalecimiento del ecosistema empresarial y el cumplimiento de metas de ingreso y participación institucional.




Tus principales retos




• Coordinar actividades de difusión de cultura emprendedora (ferias, bazares y conferencias) para fortalecer el posicionamiento de la incubadora en campus y comunidad externa.

• Organizar e impartir talleres de emprendimiento que faciliten la estructuración y validación de ideas de negocio.

• Asesorar proyectos en el desarrollo integral del plan de negocio, asegurando su correcta presentación ante comité y seguimiento en el proceso de incubación.

• Evaluar y entrevistar ideas de negocio para identificar proyectos viables y con potencial de rentabilidad.

• Gestionar inscripciones, pagos y seguimiento administrativo de proyectos para garantizar el cumplimiento del proceso institucional.

• Coordinar la participación de emprendedores en concursos internos y externos, alineando postulaciones a convocatorias vigentes.

• Elaborar y presentar informes mensuales de resultados ante directivos, impulsando estrategias para el logro de metas de ingresos y participación.

• Representar a la incubadora en eventos externos, fortaleciendo alianzas institucionales y promoviendo los servicios del centro de negocio.




Perfil que buscamos

Requisitos indispensables:




• Licenciatura en áreas Económico-Administrativas. (Título y cédula).

• 2 a 3 años de experiencia en desarrollo e implementación de planes de negocio, incubación o ejecución de proyectos empresariales, (proyectos a nivel académico)

• Conocimientos sólidos en elaboración de planes de negocio, metodologías ágiles, innovación y paquetería Office avanzada.

• Experiencia en coordinación de actividades académicas o empresariales.

• Inglés intermedio.




Deseables:

• Maestría en Desarrollo de Negocios, Innovación, Sistemas Industriales o MBA.

• Experiencia en entornos educativos o ecosistemas de emprendimiento.

• Competencias clave: pensamiento estratégico, liderazgo colaborativo, comunicación asertiva, orientación a resultados, gestión del tiempo, innovación y resolución de problemas.




Vivir en la CDMX en el sur de la Ciudad (alcaldía Coyoacán)




Tu impacto en UVM

skills: Takes lead product delivery and evaluation role for assigned signature events and projects

Serves as staff design expert for member engagement opportunities (live and virtual). Brings relevant expertise in program delivery, logistics, marketing, and engagement experience to community initiatives. Supports and assigns staff support as needed.
Ensures successful onsite/online leadership program delivery, collaboration with internal and external units, and data reports

Provides accurate and timely data reports after each iteration and year and works with the analysis team to evaluate the forum leadership products. Provides expertise during times of evaluation and gives insight into areas of improvement and trends. Maintains an active learning component to understand competitor practices and offerings.
Manage assigned products and programs from needs assessment to execution and evaluation.
Evaluate learning, forum, and community programs across the world, conducts RFPs, and manage the vendor selection process.
Serve as product owner and event organizer, requiring oversight of product data, financial records, marketing, etc.

Liaise with the products team and products portfolio to gather stakeholder input and adjust product delivery according to plan and budget. Co-design tailor-made programs that fit our members' needs and provide input to curriculum delivery, including agenda, content, and speakers. Conduct site visits as necessary.
Negotiate partnerships with Higher Education Institutions (HEI) and content providers (including international speakers and speaker bureaus).
Market products to users. Oversee registrations and member inquiries.
Evaluate programs, conduct program debriefing, suggest program improvements, and implement changes.
Track program analytics and reports.

description:
THE ORGANIZATION

The Entrepreneurs’ Organization (EO) is a high-quality support network of 20,000 business founders and owners in 220 chapters and 80 countries worldwide. EO’s purpose is to move the world forward by unlocking the full potential of entrepreneurs. Since 1987, EO has helped entrepreneurs achieve transformational growth through the power of life-enhancing connections, shared experiences, and collaborative learning. Guided by EO’s core values: trust and respect, thirst for learning, think big, be bold, and together we grow, EO’s international staff collaborates successfully across diverse cultures. As an EO employee, you will gain access to the world’s top experts in entrepreneurship, grow beyond your perceived limits, and make

breakthroughs as you refine and realize your personal goals. EO’s competitive total rewards package, flexible work environment, and generous professional development resources are frequently cited as among the most popular benefits of working at EO.

Position Summary

The Senior Manager, Product Delivery is part of the team that helps to plan, co-design, and execute global programs (in-person and hybrid) within the products department, including global learning, forum, and communities. This individual partners with top content providers and top higher education institutions and vendors; develops and executes virtual programs (such as Nano Learning, Powerhouse speakers series), and forum events, among other initiatives.

This team member adds value by acquiring and overseeing programs from start to finish, including negotiating with vendors, advocating and negotiating new partnerships, prepping speakers, HEI and service providers for our unique audience, seeing tailor-made executive education programs through to execution, and conducting needs assessments for providing training opportunities according to member challenges. They also help to deliver product trainings, signature events, and virtual programming. They serve as an advanced expert in delivery and evaluation of products and serve as a partner to key member volunteer efforts. They assist the Director with audits of programs and take an advanced role during training of staff and members as well as large-scale events.

Staying cool under stress and pressure, delivering on deadlines, demonstrating agility, creative thinking, a can- do attitude, global mindset, and a thirst for continual learning are all musts. The Senior Manager liaises with various member teams to deliver on action plans and works cooperatively with learning colleagues for a range of Products initiatives from live to virtual events.
